6102-from-jest-to-earnest.creator: Unknown

A double sleigh, overflowing with luxurious robes, stood near, and a portly coachman with difficulty restrained his spirited horses while the little party arranged themselves for a winter ride.

arxiv-2004-05937.title: Knowledge Distillation and Student-Teacher Learning for Visual Intelligence: A Review and New Outlooks
arxiv-2004-05937.creator: Lin Wang, and Kuk-Jin Yoon
arxiv-2004-05937.description: Abstract Deep neural models, in recent years, have been successful in almost every field, even solving the most complex problem statements. However, these models are huge in size with millions (and even billions) of parameters, demanding heavy computation power and failing to be deployed on edge devices. Besides, the performance boost is highly dependent on redundant labeled data.

arxiv-2011-10739.title: An introduction to hyperholomorphic spectral theories and fractional powers of vector operators
arxiv-2011-10739.creator: Fabrizio Colombo, Jonathan Gantner, Stefano Pinton
arxiv-2011-10739.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Fabrizio Colombo, Jonathan Gantner, Stefano Pinton. The aim of this paper is to give an overview of the spectral theories associated with the notions of holomorphicity in dimension greater than one. A first natural extension is the theory of several complex variables whose Cauchy formula is used to define the holomorphic functional calculus for n n -tuples of operators ( A 1 , … , A n ) (A_{1},...,A_{n}) . A second way is to consider hyperholomorphic functions of quaternionic or paravector variables.

arxiv-2201-05527.title: Federated Continual Learning for Socially Aware Robotics
arxiv-2201-05527.creator: Luke Guerdan, Hatice Gunes
arxiv-2201-05527.description: Abstract From learning assistance to companionship, socially aware and socially assistive robotics is promising for enhancing many aspects of daily life. However, socially aware robots face many challenges preventing their widespread public adoption. Two such major challenges are (1) lack in behavior adaptation to new environments, contexts and users, and (2) insufficient capability for privacy protection.

arxiv-2210-04359.title: Fine-Grained Detection of Solidarity for Women and Migrants in 155 Years of German Parliamentary Debates
arxiv-2210-04359.creator: Aida Kostikova, Benjamin Paassen, Dominik Beese, Ole Pütz, Gregor Wiedemann, Steffen Eger
arxiv-2210-04359.description: Abstract Solidarity is a crucial concept to understand social relations in societies. In this paper, we explore fine-grained solidarity frames to study solidarity towards women and migrants in German parliamentary debates between 1867 and 2022. Using 2,864 manually annotated text snippets (with a cost exceeding 18k Euro), we evaluate large language models (LLMs) like Llama 3, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4.

arxiv-2210-08063.title: On the simultaneous reconstruction of the nonlinearity coefficient and the sound speed in the Westervelt equation
arxiv-2210-08063.creator: Barbara Kaltenbacher, William Rundell
arxiv-2210-08063.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Barbara Kaltenbacher, William Rundell. This paper considers the Westervelt equation, one of the most widely used models in nonlinear acoustics, and seeks to recover two spatially-dependent parameters of physical importance from time-trace boundary measurements. Specifically, these are the nonlinearity parameter κ ⁡ ( x ) \kappa(x) often referred to as B / A B/A in the acoustics literature and the wave speed c 0 ​ ( x ) c_{0}(x) .

arxiv-2304-00911.title: Para-Sasaki-like Manifolds with Generalized Symmetric Metric Connection
arxiv-2304-00911.description: Abstract The present paper deals with the generalized symmetric metric connection defined on para-Sasaki-like manifolds. We derive a relation between the Levi-Civita connection and the generalized symmetric metric conneciton on the considered manifold. We investigate the curvature tensor, the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature tensor with respect to the generalized symmetric metric connection.

arxiv-2409-16194.title: Preparing Ground and Excited States Using Adiabatic CoVaR
arxiv-2409-16194.creator: Wooseop Hwang, Bálint Koczor
arxiv-2409-16194.description: Abstract CoVarince Root finding with classical shadows (CoVaR) was recently introduced as a new paradigm for training variational quantum circuits. Common approaches, such as variants of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver, aim to optimise a non-linear classical cost function and thus suffer from, e.g., poor local minima, high shot requirements and barren plateaus.

arxiv-2410-23376.title: Storage and retrieval of two unknown unitary channels
arxiv-2410-23376.creator: Michal Sedlák, Robert Stárek, Nikola Horová, Michal Mičuda, Jaromir Fiurášek, Alessandro Bisio
arxiv-2410-23376.description: Abstract We address the fundamental task of converting n n uses of an unknown unitary transformation into a quantum state (i.e., storage) and later retrieval of the transformation. Specifically, we consider the case where the unknown unitary is selected with equal prior probability from two options.

arxiv-2504-19986.creator: Andrés F. Andrews, Marcelo Barraza-Alfaro, Gianni Cataldi, Nicolás Cuello, Ian Czekala, Daniele Fasano, Mario
arxiv-2504-19986.description: Abstract The ALMA large program exoALMA offers a unique window into the three-dimensional physical and dynamical properties of 15 circumstellar discs where planets may be actively forming. Here, we present an analysis methodology to map the gas disc structure and substructure encoded in 12 CO, 13 CO, and CS line emission from our targets.

arxiv-2505-08794.title: Classical Dirac particle I
arxiv-2505-08794.creator: Martín Rivas
arxiv-2505-08794.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Martín Rivas. In this work we produce a classical Lagrangian description of an elementary spinning particle which satisfies Dirac equation when quantized. We call this particle a classical Dirac particle . We analyze in detail the way we arrive to this model and how the different observables and constants of the motion can be expressed in terms of the degrees of freedom and their derivatives, by making use of Noether’s theorem.

pmc-10629678.title: The chromatin source-sink hypothesis: a shared mode of chromatin-mediated regulations
pmc-10629678.creator: Patrick J Murphy, Frédéric Berger
pmc-10629678.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We propose that several chromatin-mediated regulatory processes are dominated by source-sink relationships in which factors operate as ‘sources’ to produce or provide a resource and compete with each other to occupy separate ‘sinks’. In this model, large portions of genomic DNA operate as ‘sinks’, which are filled by ‘sources’, such as available histone variants, covalent modifications to histones, the readers of these modifications and non-coding RNAs.

pmc-11381906.description: Kinetoplastid organisms, including Trypanosoma brucei, are a significant health burden in many tropical and semitropical countries. Much of their metabolism is poorly understood. To better study kinetoplastid metabolism, chemical probes that inhibit kinetoplastid enzymes are needed. To discover chemical probes, we have developed a high-throughput flow cytometry screening assay that simultaneously measures multiple glycolysis-relevant metabolites in live T.

pmc-11507054.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Cellular Heterogeneity and Drivers in Serrated Pathway-Driven Colorectal Cancer Progression
pmc-11507054.creator: Jiahui Wang, Yu Zhang, Xinyi Chen, Qi Sheng, Junluo Yang, Yuyao Zhu, Yuhang Wang, Fangrong Yan, Jingya Fang, Carmine Stolfi
pmc-11507054.description: Serrated lesions are common precancerous pathways in colorectal cancer (CRC), but the process by which they progress to malignancy remains unclear. We aimed to elucidate this progression through a single-cell RNA landscape. We conducted single-cell RNA sequencing on three normal colonic tissues and fifteen SLs (including HPs, SSLs, SSLD, and TSAs) and integrated these data with datasets containing tumor samples.

pmc-11648942.creator: Yinong Zhao, Xingfei Wei, Rigoberto Hernandez
pmc-11648942.description: Nanoparticle networks have potential applications in brain-like computing yet their ability to adopt different states remains unexplored. pmc-11782143.title: Spatial variations in the microbiota: comparative analysis of microbial composition and predicted functions across different intestinal segments and feces in donkeys
pmc-11782143.creator: Yanwei Wang, Tong Hu, Kaixuan Liang, Shinuo Li, Qiyue Zhang, Wenqiang Li, Honglei Qu, Boying Dong, Haihua Zhang, Qiugang Ma, Ru Jia, Shimeng Huang
pmc-11782143.description: Donkeys, as single-stomach herbivores, have a complex and diverse microbial community in their digestive tracts. The intestinal bacterial community is crucial for maintaining intestinal homeostasis, as well as the host’s overall nutrition and health. However, research on donkey gut microbes is relatively limited, particularly regarding the microbial colonization patterns in different intestinal segments of adult donkeys.

pmc-13011355.title: Soluble cytokines and chemokines in NSCLC: drivers of immune evasion and angiogenesis
pmc-13011355.creator: Liang Yang, Zhijun Fan, Zhe Wang, Dong Zhou
pmc-13011355.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The tumor microenvironment (TME) is characterized by a dynamic network of soluble cytokines and chemokines that orchestrate immune evasion, promote angiogenesis, and facilitate metastatic dissemination. Among these, interleukins such as IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10, along with chemokine axes including CXCL12–CXCR4 and CCL21–CCR7, are critical drivers of tumor progression and resistance to immunotherapy.

pmc-13443745.creator: Zulfadli Mahfodz, Rahmat Dapari, Siti Aekbal Salleh, Siti Nazrina Camalxaman, Marzani Mohammad Yusop, Nazri Che Dom
